chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Bird leaves for Earl Hines
summary: Bird left in 1943 for Earl Hines after Andy Kirk took him to New York; Hines promised to straighten him out and soon begged McShann to take him back.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Because I remember one night, he told me just as plain, you know, when things would get tight --
Just one second, Jay. He must have left in '43 because he was with Earl in '43. That's what they all were saying, because of the record ban, they didn't make any records. He was with Earl.

Well, here's what. He left me in '43 and joined Earl. See, I let him go in the Paradise Theater in Detroit and then here's what happened. Andy Kirk was playing in town and Andy took him all the way back to New York. We was in New York two weeks. He got to New York a week before we did, Bird with Andy. So I run into Earl Hines. Earl Hines told me, he says, 'Now, I'll tell you something. Now, I talked to Charlie and Charlie's coming on with the group. Now, I'm going to tell you something. I'll make a man out of him. I'll show you something. Now, you don't know how to handle these guys. You don't know how to handle them. I'll take him and I'll make
a man out of him." I says, "Okay."
Three months later, I saw Earl Hines and Earl Hines was screaming to me, "Come and get this man. Get this man away from me. That's the worst man I've ever seen in my life."

"I've never seen anything go down like that. See, he owes everybody, every loan shark in town. Owes everybody over there at the Parlor Theater, owes everybody in the band. He's -- I bought him a brand new horn and he's so bad, --" you know.
